breaking.headline: Anthropic closes first day at $97.17, still 17% above its IPO price
breaking.fact: Anthropic closed its first day on the Nasdaq at $97.17 Thursday — up 17.07% from its $83 IPO price, but 12.9% below its $111.50 opening trade after touching $115.10. The $81.3 billion offering is the largest IPO on record, and the fully diluted value closed near $1.75 trillion on volume of more than 846 million shares. Sean’s 66 shares at $83 are now worth $6,413.22.

breaking.headline: Stocks close sharply lower; Dow falls below 50,000, S&P logs sixth straight loss
breaking.fact: The Dow fell 1,101.11 points, or 2.19%, to 49,097.06 — its first close below 50,000 since June — while the S&P 500 dropped 2.02% to 7,175.83 for a sixth straight loss, its longest slide in about two and a half years, and the Nasdaq fell 2.25% to 23,879.20. All seven Magnificent Seven stocks finished lower, the S&P is on course for its steepest weekly decline since April 2025, and the VIX closed at 28.44.

breaking.headline: Williams-Sonoma plunges 15% after sales miss — worst in the S&P 500
breaking.fact: Williams-Sonoma fell 15.16% to $220.66, the worst performer in the S&P 500, after third-quarter revenue of $1.99 billion came in just short of the $2 billion consensus, even though adjusted earnings of $2.19 a share matched estimates. The company only reiterated its full-year outlook rather than raising it, and flagged fourth-quarter cost pressure from oil-driven freight costs.

breaking.headline: Fed minutes point to more hikes; December increase now nearly certain
breaking.fact: Minutes of the Fed’s October 27–28 meeting, released Wednesday, show ‘almost all’ officials judged further rate increases ‘would likely be appropriate,’ with a couple floating a larger-than-25-basis-point move in December if inflation data stay hot. Traders price a quarter-point December hike at about 92–95%, with roughly an 8% chance of a half-point move; JPMorgan expects three more hikes — December, January and March — taking the target range to 4.50%–4.75%, and the dollar index hit a 19-month high near 104.

weekInBrief.headline: IEA: Hormuz crisis is the largest energy supply shock on record
weekInBrief.body: The International Energy Agency’s World Energy Outlook 2026, published Thursday, puts the oil and gas lost to the Hormuz crisis at 2.8 billion barrels and 60 billion cubic metres by end-October — the largest supply shock the world has faced. In its ‘Low Hormuz’ case, oil flows through the strait fall from 20 million barrels a day before the crisis to 8.5 million by 2030 and under 2 million by 2035 as bypass pipelines and alternative supplies take over, though the Middle East would remain the world’s largest oil exporter. Executive Director Fatih Birol said he sees ‘no credible pathway’ for the energy world to return to the way it was before.

weekInBrief.headline: Alibaba’s AI cloud jumps 53%, but cash burn deepens and earnings miss
weekInBrief.body: Alibaba reported September-quarter revenue of 271.5 billion yuan ($40.5 billion), up 10% and just ahead of estimates, with AI cloud and compute revenue up 53% to 61 billion yuan and AI-related product revenue growing triple digits for a 13th straight quarter. Reported profit more than tripled to 64.5 billion yuan on investment gains, but adjusted earnings of 8.10 yuan per ADS missed the 10.75 yuan analysts expected, free cash flow was a 34.5 billion yuan outflow as capital spending jumped 60%, and CEO Eddie Wu said new U.S. chip rules may force a cut to the company’s 20-gigawatt data-center goal.

weekInBrief.headline: Mortgage rates jump to 7.28%, ending a four-week slide
weekInBrief.body: The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate rose to 7.28% in Freddie Mac’s weekly survey released Thursday, up 17 basis points from 7.11% last week and from 6.26% a year ago — the first weekly increase since early October, ending a four-week streak of declines. The 15-year fixed rose to 6.66%. The jump follows the Fed’s hawkish October minutes, which have traders pricing a December rate hike as nearly certain; daily measures put the 30-year near 7.45%.

weekInBrief.headline: APEC summit opens in Shenzhen with Xi, Trump and Putin in attendance
weekInBrief.body: The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting opened Thursday in Shenzhen, China, with Presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin addressing leaders from 21 member economies amid concerns over global trade, energy security and rising geopolitical tensions. Xi called for stronger regional trade ties and announced $20 million in support for Asia-Pacific cooperation, while Trump highlighted U.S. economic strength and AI leadership and opposed global AI regulation.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Iran’s army claimed on Wednesday evening that three more oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire east of the Strait of Hormuz after switching off their navigation systems in a declared exclusion zone — but it named no vessels, and Reuters could not independently verify the claim; the Revolutionary Guards separately claim six tankers have been mined since Sunday. A confirmed attack on an ADNOC vessel on Tuesday evening left 11 crew injured and one missing, according to UKMTO. The U.S. blockade’s tightened enforcement rules, circulated to shipowners as JMIC Advisory 017-26, now treat any vessel receiving Iranian cargo in a ship-to-ship transfer as a blockade evader, subject to being stopped, boarded or seized. On oil, the blockade still holds — Iranian crude exports have remained near a standstill for months, shipping sources told Reuters, while Kpler puts total oil and product flows through the strait at about 8.3 million barrels a day in the week to November 11, roughly 48% of pre-war levels.

space.headline: Musk outlines a bigger Starship V4 after Saturday’s first orbital catch
space.body: Elon Musk said Thursday that Starship V4 will be about 70 metres long — roughly 40% bigger than V3 — with more than 60% additional propellant and higher-thrust Raptor engines, after SpaceX’s Starship upper stage was caught by the launch tower’s arms on Saturday following a 22-hour orbital flight, the first such catch after a trip to orbit. Musk said a reusable Starship could carry 200 metric tons to orbit and that refuelling costs could fall to $500,000. The booster was lost on the same flight, and SpaceX expects to begin Starship launches from Florida’s Kennedy Space Center within the next few months.

space.headline: ULA’s Vulcan fails to reach orbit with 40 Amazon satellites
space.body: United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket failed to reach orbit on Sunday carrying 40 Amazon Leo communications satellites, a setback for the Boeing-Lockheed Martin joint venture’s new heavy launcher. The Planetary Society’s analysis Thursday contrasts the failure with SpaceX’s Starship triumph a day earlier: the world’s largest rocket hit a historic milestone while the more conventional approach fell short, underscoring how lopsided the U.S. launch industry has become, with government and commercial customers functionally dependent on a single company.

space.headline: Electric currents switch antiferromagnets at room temperature
space.body: Researchers led by Northwestern Engineering have discovered an effect — octupole-driven spin-transfer torque — that lets an electric current manipulate the magnetic state of noncollinear antiferromagnets at room temperature, in nanoscale devices built from two antiferromagnetic layers separated by a thin insulating barrier. The work, published in Nature, could open a path to faster, more robust magnetic memory that is immune to stray magnetic fields.

space.headline: Neutron scans reveal a tiny horned reptile from 156 million years ago
space.body: Neutron imaging at the Paul Scherrer Institute has revealed a previously unknown species of horned reptile from a fossil found in a Wyoming quarry in 2022. Named Meilynodraco amonamarthi, the 156-million-year-old animal is the most complete early-branching choristodere known and the oldest record of the group in North America. The findings are published in Royal Society Open Science, and the little ‘dragon’ will feature in a travelling exhibition at the Aathal Dinosaur Museum in early 2027.

apod.title: Empire State Building Goes Gold for Voyager
apod.credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls — NASA Image of the Day, November 18, 2026
apod.explanation: The Empire State Building is seen illuminated in gold to celebrate NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft as it was about to pass one light-day away from Earth — a distance reached by no other human-made object — on November 17, 2026. The gold honours the gold-plated copper phonograph record flying aboard Voyager, the Golden Record carrying sounds and images chosen to portray the diversity of life and culture on Earth.
